sources.entry: 🏙 Move fast and don't break things, Google

summary.title: Move Fast & Don't Break Things
summary.one_liner: A GTAC 2014 slide deck by Google's Ankit Mehta on balancing development velocity with software quality through test engineering.
keywords: move fast and don't break things
how google balances release speed and quality
takeaways: Test engineering's purpose at Google is framed as building world-class infrastructure so teams can launch high-quality products quickly.
Google's scale is cited as 30K check-ins per day (a check-in every 3 seconds) and 2x more releases.
Long release cycles create pressure to get changes in, which leads to regressions and further delays.
Moving fast brings innovation, faster fixes, productivity and code health, but breaking things erodes user trust and the brand.
The deck contrasts common team testing practices (maintenance burden, slower tests, flakiness) with how testing should be done.
summary.summary: This is a slide deck from a GTAC 2014 talk by Ankit Mehta of Google about balancing release velocity with product quality. It opens with the speaker's background in test engineering and frames the purpose of test engineering as building infrastructure that lets teams launch high-quality products fast. It then uses Google-scale figures (30K check-ins per day, 2x more releases) and describes problems with long release cycles, such as regressions and delays. The final slides contrast common testing practices (maintenance burden, slow tests, flakiness) with the recommended approach. The page text is mostly slide titles and bullets, so the detailed reasoning behind the recommendations is not fully present.
